requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
rationale:
The requirement has two obligations. The first is that a `habeas` skill is bundled. The second is that its description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project and names four signs of one: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code.

The marked test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_used_at_the_start_of_any_work_in_a_habeas_project]` covers both.

- **Bundling:** The helper `skill_files` embeds `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` with `include_str!`. So the test reads the skill file that is actually bundled, and it would fail to compile if the file were missing.
- **Description lookup:** The helper `description` extracts the front-matter `description: ` line and panics if there is none.
- **Start-of-work instruction:** The test asserts the description starts with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas".
- **Four signs:** The test loops over the four signs and asserts that the description contains each one. The loop's failure message prints the missing sign.

The real description in `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` contains all of this text, so the assertions match the requirement and check it.

The assertions are string-level. They can't confirm that the description "tells agents" anything beyond its wording, but that is the only observable form of the obligation. No other branch or mode needs separate testing.
